explanation: King Solomon, son of King David, who built the first temple in Jerusalem to house the Ark of the Covenant and honor God.
A holy place in Jerusalem where the Israelites worshiped God and performed religious ceremonies; built by King Solomon as a dwelling for God's presence.
A country in the Middle East, known for its cedar trees; Solomon obtained cedars from Lebanon to use in building the temple.
A precious metal symbolizing wealth and divinity; used abundantly in the construction of the temple to show respect and reverence for God.
A gold-covered chest containing the two stone tablets with the Ten Commandments, a symbolic representation of God's covenant with the people of Israel.
Supernatural beings, often described as winged creatures, who served as guardians and attendants to God; two large cherubs were made of gold and placed in the Most Holy Place of the temple.

The innermost and most sacred room of the temple, where the Ark of the Covenant was kept and where the high priest entered once a year on the Day of Atonement to ask for forgiveness for the nation's sins.
